name: John Tuthill

residences.note: A 'John Tuthill' signed the 1775 Articles of Association in Cornwall Precinct. This is either this man (if he outlived Alva Tuttle's c.1770 death) or his son John (b. 1753)

bioAdditions:
Two new pieces bear on John's life. First, a 'John Tuthill' signed the 1775 Articles of Association in Cornwall Precinct, on the same list as 'James Tuttle' and Thomas Lamoureux (S3). Either John was still alive in 1775, which would undercut Alva Tuttle's c.1770 death and partly vindicate the tree's later death date, or the signer was his son John (b. 1753). Second, the Brookhaven town records show the family's Long Island base. James Tuthill, John's probable father, held the westernmost 15-acre lot in Fireplace Neck by 1737 (S2). That is a few miles from Moriches, where Temperance Smith's father James Smith lived, so the two families were close neighbours.

The printed pre-1784 New York marriage-license list has no Tuthill-Smith entry (S4), and the NY will abstracts to 1784 hold no will or administration for him (S6). The 23 Nov 1752 Smithtown marriage date therefore still rests on Alva Tuttle alone. It is repeated without sources by Long Island Surnames (S5) and in an Ancestry compiled index cited on WikiTree.

conflicts.foundValue: A John Tuthill signed in Cornwall Precinct in 1775
conflicts.assessment: Not decisive, because son John (b. 1753) was of age by 1775. Keep c.1770 as Alva's estimate, but note that 1775 is possible.

relationships.evidence: Unchanged: rests on Alva Tuttle p. 311 ('s Jas 1692'). New context: James Tuthill owned land in Fireplace Neck, Brookhaven, 1721-1750, and a 'James Tuttle junr.' appears there c.1738/9, consistent with Alva's son James b. 1717.
